botDocs.title: IDEL bot API
botDocs.subtitle: The bot runs on your side: it receives messages via long-polling and replies on its own behalf. The server never runs your code.
botDocs.tokenHint: Never share the token — it grants full access to the bot. Rotate it in @creatorbot: /newtoken <number>.
botDocs.limits: Limits: 60 requests per minute and 20 messages per minute. On exceeding you get 429 with a Retry-After header.
botDocs.rule1: A bot may only write to users who wrote to it first.
botDocs.rule2: No moderation powers: warnings, bans and badges are unavailable to bots.
botDocs.rule3: Bot messages and posts pass the same profanity filter.
botDocs.rule4: Replies come in the updates array together with nextOffset — pass it to the next request.
botDocs.authTitle: Signing in to a user profile
botDocs.authHint: A bot may request access to an account. The confirmation code is delivered to the user's chat with @resendcode_bot — not by email.
botDocs.authStep1: The bot sends the user's username or email plus the list of capabilities it needs: POST /api/bot/auth/request.
botDocs.authStep2: The user receives a code from @resendcode_bot stating which bot asks for access and what it will be able to do.
botDocs.authStep3: The user hands the code to the bot, the bot confirms it: POST /api/bot/auth/confirm — and receives a 30-minute grant.
botDocs.authStep4: Actions are limited to the declared capabilities. The user sees a “Bot sign-in” session in settings and can end it — the grant stops working immediately.
botDocs.webhookHint: Instead of polling, the server POSTs events to your URL. Perfect for Flask bots: the app receives the event, verifies the signature and replies through the API.
botDocs.webhookRetry: If the webhook does not answer 2xx, the server retries (3 attempts) and then puts the event into the long-polling queue — the bot can fetch it with bot.updates().
botDocs.exampleHint: idelbot.py and the example bot live in the bot-api folder of the repository. No external dependencies.
botDocs.moreBots: Need another bot or a new token? @creatorbot does all of that.
